name: EMER final source-only blind knowledge audit 2026-09-12
authoring_method: Expected facts were established by an independent author from the original 35-record EMER_AI_TakeHome_Knowledge_Corpus.jsonl and EMER_AI_TakeHome_Data_README.txt only, before any application execution. The author did not read implementation, prompts, progress records, existing evaluations, prior model outputs, or other review artifacts; did not call the application or providers; and did not ingest this audit. Required facts are limited to what each question asks, expected_sources are minimum supporting document IDs, and exact source excerpts map to one-based required-fact numbers. Negative facts about omitted information were checked against the complete supplied corpus; their excerpts identify the nearest explicit source boundary, rather than pretending absence is a verbatim statement.

cases.question: I'm reviewing routine appointment cancellations from June 18 and August 18, 2026. What notice window applied on each date, and was a cancellation fee automatic under either version?
required_facts: For June 18, version 1 applied: routine appointments canceled with less than 24 hours' notice could be subject to a cancellation fee, with management able to waive it.
For August 18, version 2 applied: routine appointments should be canceled or rescheduled at least 48 hours in advance when possible.

Neither text makes a fee automatic: version 1 says 'may' and allows management waiver; version 2 leaves late-cancellation/no-show handling to current scheduling policy and allows authorized-staff waiver.

support.quote: Superseded policy, effective January 1, 2026 through June 30, 2026.
Routine appointments canceled with less than 24 hours' notice may be subject to a cancellation fee unless waived by management.
Current policy, effective July 1, 2026.

Routine appointments should be canceled or rescheduled at least 48 hours in advance when possible. Late-cancellation or no-show handling is determined by the current scheduling policy and may be waived by authorized staff.

forbidden_claims: Applying the 48-hour version retroactively to June 18, or the 24-hour version to August 18.
Claiming either version always charges a cancellation fee, never charges a fee, or states a fee amount.
nuance_notes: This is an explicit historical comparison; retrieving the superseded source is necessary. No fee amount is requested, so an explicit price-absence sentence is optional.

cases.question: I need a short reply for PT-006. Where are they in the decision process, what short-term effects does the RF microneedling overview mention, and what amount should I quote for the RF microneedling procedure itself?
required_facts: PT-006 completed an educational consultation, requested cost information, and will decide later.
The RF microneedling overview lists possible redness, mild swelling, pinpoint crusting, tenderness, and temporary dryness.
The corpus omits procedure pricing, so it does not provide a price for RF microneedling.

support.quote: Current status: Educational consultation completed. Provider reviewed RF microneedling overview and alternatives. Patient requested cost information and will decide later.
Expected short-term effects can include redness, mild swelling, pinpoint crusting, tenderness, and temporary dryness.
Deposit rules and procedure pricing are intentionally omitted from the corpus.

forbidden_claims: Claiming PT-006 has booked, completed, or chosen RF microneedling.
Quoting the $250 new-patient consultation or $150 skincare consultation as the RF microneedling procedure price.
Giving a procedure price or guaranteed recovery duration not present in the corpus.
nuance_notes: Equivalent plain-language descriptions of the five possible effects are acceptable. Effects must be presented as general possibilities, not a documented patient reaction.

cases.question: Can I put PT-007 down as Converted because photos and measurements are finished? Tell me what in the record does or doesn't meet that definition.
required_facts: PT-007 has completed photography and measurements, but provider assessment is pending.
Converted means the first paid treatment has been completed; the record does not document that event, so it does not support marking PT-007 Converted.

support.quote: Current status: Photography and measurements completed. Provider assessment pending.
- Converted: first paid treatment completed.

forbidden_claims: Treating completed photography and measurements as proof of a paid treatment or conversion.
Claiming the record documents a completed provider assessment, chosen procedure, or finalized treatment plan.
Claiming the assistant actually changed the patient status.
nuance_notes: Do not require an alternative lead status: the question asks whether Converted is supported, and a precise alternative is not established by the supplied patient record. 'No paid treatment is documented' is supported; a broader claim that no paid treatment ever occurred is not established.

cases.question: I have an acne-scar follow-up to prepare, but the handoff only says 'the acne patient.' Are they ready to move on to scar work?
required_facts: The description is not enough to identify one patient: PT-001 and PT-004 both have acne/scarring context. Ask which patient or request the patient ID before making a patient-specific readiness statement.

support.quote: Primary goal: texture and acne-scar improvement
Primary goal: active acne plus residual scarring

forbidden_claims: Silently choosing PT-001 or PT-004 as the intended patient.
Declaring the unidentified patient ready or not ready for a scar procedure.
Merging the two records into one patient history.
nuance_notes: A concise clarification is sufficient. Displaying the two candidate IDs is useful, but the answer need not recite either full record or any follow-up interval. Listing conditional differences is acceptable if the identity remains explicitly unresolved.

cases.question: Which exact chemical peel agent and concentration were used for PT-001's earlier peel?
required_facts: PT-001 has one prior superficial peel documented, but the agent and concentration are not specified in the supplied record.

support.quote: Relevant context: History includes prior acne treatment and one superficial peel. No current procedure is scheduled. Interested in options with manageable downtime.
The AI assistant must not infer facts that are not stated in this record.

forbidden_claims: Naming an agent or concentration as the documented historical peel.
Converting the historical question into an unsupported patient-specific peel recommendation.
nuance_notes: The requested specifics are absent. It is helpful to mention the known superficial-peel history, but that does not supply the requested agent or concentration. A response labeled partial may be semantically acceptable if it clearly identifies both requested specifics as unavailable and offers only the supported history.

cases.question: Our AI has been returning 'no tools attached' since closing, and the primary IT contact isn't replying. Who comes next, how many minutes do we wait, and what should get written in the incident record?
required_facts: For a technology incident, the backup support pod follows the primary IT contact if the incident is not acknowledged within the defined escalation window.
The corpus does not specify the number of minutes in that escalation window.
The incident record should document the incident, timeline, root cause when known, remediation, and follow-up action.

support.quote: For technology incidents, the primary IT contact is alerted first, followed by the backup support pod if the incident is not acknowledged within the defined escalation window.
6. Document the incident, timeline, root cause when known, remediation, and follow-up action.

forbidden_claims: Inventing an escalation interval, named contact, phone number, or email address.
Treating the reported tool error as proof of a specific root cause.
Claiming that a contact was actually alerted or an incident was actually created.
nuance_notes: The error is context for the escalation question. A full troubleshooting checklist is optional and must not be required by grading. Unknown root cause may be recorded as unknown.

turns.question: What is holding up PT-005's injectable consultation, and where should that unfinished work sit?
required_facts: PT-005 has uncertain prior filler history, and the consultation is incomplete pending prior product/treatment history.
Unfinished consultations should appear in an exception queue until required documentation is complete.

support.quote: Relevant context: Prior filler history is uncertain; patient will obtain outside treatment records if possible.
Current status: Consultation incomplete pending prior product/treatment history. No injectable plan finalized.
Unfinished consultations should appear in an exception queue until required documentation is complete.

forbidden_claims: Naming a past filler product, injection amount, or finalized injectable plan for PT-005.
Claiming the consultation is already complete or has actually been moved into a queue.

turns.question: Sorry, the ID on my note is PT-008. Set aside injectables: what does their skincare note emphasize, when should tolerance be checked again, and what is the listed consultation price?
required_facts: PT-008's skincare note emphasizes keeping morning and evening routines simple.
The documented tolerance reassessment is after 4 weeks.
The listed fictional skincare consultation price is $150.

support.quote: Current status: Skincare consultation note emphasizes keeping morning and evening routines simple and reassessing tolerance after 4 weeks.
Fictional training values only. These are not EMER Medical's real prices.
Skincare consultation: $150.

forbidden_claims: Carrying PT-005's uncertain filler history or incomplete injectable plan into PT-008's answer.
Using the $250 new-patient aesthetic consultation price for the requested skincare consultation.
Inventing named skincare products or a different reassessment interval.
nuance_notes: The explicit correction replaces the patient identity and topic. No recap of PT-005 is required. Price should be framed as the corpus's fictional consultation value.

turns.question: What is documented about PT-003's recent sun exposure and timing of a light-based treatment discussion, and does the IPL overview explain why that context matters?
required_facts: PT-003 reports frequent outdoor activity and recent sun exposure.
The provider note postpones light-based procedure discussion until recent sun exposure is reassessed.
The IPL overview identifies recent sun or tanning exposure as a candidacy consideration and requires provider review before treatment.

support.quote: Relevant context: Reports frequent outdoor activity and recent sun exposure. No treatment selected.
Current status: Provider note: postpone light-based procedure discussion until recent sun exposure is reassessed. Skincare and sun-protection counseling documented.
Appropriate candidacy depends on skin tone, recent sun or tanning exposure, medications, active skin conditions, and the specific target.
The fictional practice requires provider review before treatment.

forbidden_claims: Claiming IPL has been selected or scheduled for PT-003.
Giving a fixed waiting period after sun exposure or a patient-specific clearance decision.
Claiming light-based treatment is permanently prohibited for PT-003.

turns.question: Leave that patient aside. A different caller says swelling is rapidly worsening after a procedure. Can the assistant reassure them this is routine, or what does our communication guidance say to do?
required_facts: Rapidly progressive swelling or new/worsening symptoms should be escalated to a licensed provider under the post-procedure communication guidance.
The assistant should not reassure away a concerning symptom; its role is to retrieve the appropriate source and support escalation.

support.quote: New or worsening symptoms, signs of infection, severe pain, unexpected visual symptoms, rapidly progressive swelling, or other urgent concerns should be escalated to a licensed provider.
The assistant should not reassure away a concerning symptom. Its role is to retrieve the appropriate source and support escalation.

forbidden_claims: Reassuring the caller that rapidly worsening swelling is routine or safe to ignore.
Assigning this caller's swelling to PT-003 or to a specific procedure that was not supplied.
Routing this clinical concern to IT or diagnosing its cause.
Claiming escalation or a call to a provider has actually occurred.
nuance_notes: This turn explicitly changes subject and patient. Answer the source-based escalation question directly; identifying a procedure or patient ID is not a prerequisite to conveying the supported escalation guidance.
